title: GiveDirectly's hybrid MobileAid program in Malawi may have enrolled 35% of recipients by phone-metadata machine learning and halved enrollment cost
summary: GiveDirectly posts (2024-2025) describe phone-metadata AI/ML targeting in Malawi: 35% of recipients enrolled via phone data, cost per enrolee halved; no date, count or independent source.
account: GiveDirectly's MobileAid approach uses machine learning on mobile-phone usage patterns to identify people in need and pay them by mobile money. Its 4 September 2025 post (Vera Lummis) states that it has evaluated the method across four countries since 2021 (Togo, DRC, Malawi and Bangladesh), that in Malawi it ran a hybrid program identifying and enrolling 35% of recipients via phone metadata and 65% in person, that this halved the cost of identifying and enrolling each additional person compared with a fully in-person operation, that it is working with the Government of Malawi to fill gaps in the urban social registry with phone metadata, and that a study with the Government of Malawi, U.C. Berkeley and U.C. San Diego on whether phone metadata can flag people whose poverty deepens after a shock is expected to report in 2026. Its 27 January 2025 post (Nirali Desai and Vera Lummis) describes interviews with 67 recipients across Malawi and Kenya in February and October 2024 on how to explain the AI/ML targeting, naming Mzuzu, and finds scenario-based explanations most understandable. No fetched source gives the Malawi program's dates, location, number of recipients or an independent evaluation, so the date observed is the MobileAid post's publication date.
purpose: Identify people in poverty from mobile-phone metadata with machine learning so that cash can be delivered faster and more cheaply; the claimed benefit (cheaper, faster enrollment) is that purpose.
system: GiveDirectly MobileAid: machine-learning poverty targeting from mobile-phone metadata
developer: GiveDirectly (MobileAid), with research partners; for the Malawi study the Government of Malawi, U.C. Berkeley and U.C. San Diego
deployer: GiveDirectly, with the Government of Malawi for the urban social registry work
segment: Non-governmental cash-transfer organization working with a national government

ai_role.statement: Only the maker's account was fetched. GiveDirectly states that machine learning on phone metadata identified and enrolled 35% of recipients in a Malawi hybrid program and halved the cost per additional enrolee; it gives no date, place, recipient count or accuracy for Malawi, and the Government of Malawi, U.C. Berkeley and U.C. San Diego study is described as pending (findings expected in 2026). The earlier verifier found the same: the explain-AI page names no deployment, date or outcome.

Kenya: enrollment in flood- and drought-prone areas with Safaricom processing phone metadata in-house, described as ongoing
